articles.headline: Royals snap a 5-game skid with a 5-4 win over White Sox, delaying Chicago's bid for a playoff berth
articles.description: — Miguel Garcia had three hits and three RBI, including a tiebreaking, run-scoring double in the seventh inning, as the Kansas City Royals beat the White Sox 5-4 Wednesday night and delayed Chicago's bid for a postseason berth.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — Miguel Garcia had three hits and three RBI, including a tiebreaking, run-scoring double in the seventh inning, as the Kansas City Royals beat the White Sox 5-4 Wednesday night and delayed Chicago's bid for a postseason berth.


              Chicago could have secured its first playoff berth since 2021 with a win over the Royals and a Texas loss to the New York Mets.


              Instead, Garcia and the Royals played the role of spoiler.


              Connor Thomas (2-1) struck out one and allowed one hit in two scoreless innings for the win. Steven Cruz struck out two in the ninth and earned his eighth save.


              Kansas City had three straight singles to open the bottom of the first and Garcia drove in two runs with a single to right. Vinnie Pasquantino followed with a double that scored Garcia. Pasquantino made it 4-0, scoring on shortstop Colson Montgomery’s throwing error.


              Chicago opener Bryan Hudson recorded just one out while facing five batters and allowing four runs, three earned.


              The White Sox responded with five hits in the third inning — including Kyle Teel’s two-run single and RBI hits by Miguel Vargas and Munetaka Murakami — sending 10 batters to the plate and tying the score at 4.


              In his final start of the season, Kansas City's Seth Lugo allowed four runs on seven hits, striking out three in 3 1/3 innings. His 200 hits allowed lead the American League and his 99 earned runs allowed rank second.


              Carter Jensen had three singles for the Royals (68-90), who snapped a five-game skid.


              Braden Montgomery had three singles as the White Sox (81-77) remained one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians (82-76), who lost 1-0 to Boston.


              Hagen Smith (3-3), the fourth of five Chicago pitchers, allowed a pair of hits and one run in the seventh.


              Up next
              The White Sox have not named a starter for Thursday's series finale. Royals RHP Randy Dobnak (3-4, 3.08 ERA) gets the start.

articles.headline: Harrison Jr. blocking out noise amid slow start for Cardinals
articles.description: Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.

Harrison, who has one catch for 33 yards on four targets through two games this season, said Wednesday that he's not surprised by the reaction to his slow start, but said it hasn't been difficult to keep his confidence high. He didn't hesitate when asked where his confidence level is, saying he has "a lot of confidence in myself."

"Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn't going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from.

"And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said Wednesday that "nobody has lost confidence in Marv" despite his start to the season, while Harrison didn't shy away from the reality his season has gotten off to a slow and citing a number of reasons.

"It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really.

"So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general."

Another reason, Harrison said, is because of the two defenses he's played this season. The Los Angeles Chargers gave him single coverage on just seven of 32 routes and the Seattle Seahawks are, simply, one of the best defenses in the NFL.

"Pretty much that simple," Harrison said. "Seattle's a really good defense and you don't want to give a lot of teams, especially a rival team, a lot of credit. But when you just look across the league, they're far beyond above everybody else, especially on the defensive side of the football. So, things like that happen."

Brissett said the two have had "good conversations" and has tried to lend an ear to Harrison whenever he needs it.

"It's easy to say, 'Oh, it's a long season' to other people, but to Marv it doesn't feel like it's a long season," Brissett said. "As a teammate and as a quarterback, you still have to be there for him because what if this week goes the same way? Am I just going to not be there? It's a new week and that's the benefit of it being so early in the season that you have multiple weeks to hopefully be out there and just be able to do better."

articles.body:
Manchester United have identified a new potential replacement for left back Luke Shaw. Plus, Erling Haaland is contracted to Manchester City for another eight years, but could Bayern Munich sign him? Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Liverpool are interested in Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils reportedly see the 27-year-old as an alternative to Newcastle United's Lewis Hall as they continue plans to identify a long-term successor to Luke Shaw. Mitchell entered the final 12 months of his contract in the summer, and it is said that Chelsea are also monitoring his situation, attracted to the opportunity of landing him on a free transfer.

- Bayern Munich have emerged as suitors for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are believed to see the 26-year-old as a potential future replacement for Harry Kane, who they want to remain at the Allianz Arena for a further two years before assessing whether a move for Haaland is possible. Meanwhile, TEAMtalk reports that Vincent Kompany's side are also keen on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, and could be contenders for his signature next summer amid plans to add him to their squad with England compatriot Kane.

- Chelsea and Manchester City are exploring a move for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda, according to TEAMtalk. The Blues are said to have tracked the 19-year-old for some time, and they are monitoring whether an opportunity to land him could arise due to a lack of minutes for the Rossoneri since returning from his loan spell at Lecce. Camarda scored one goal in 21 Serie A appearances last season.

- Napoli are struggling to make progress in talks with the representatives of midfielder Kevin De Bruyne over a new contract, transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports. Discussions have reportedly stalled with the 35-year-old, who arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on a two-year deal in the summer of 2025, and it is now said that they are "on the verge" of parting ways next summer. De Bruyne was previously linked with clubs in Major League Soccer and the Saudi Pro League before deciding to join Gli Azzurri.

- On-loan Aston Villa winger Alejandro Garnacho is attracting interest from clubs in LaLiga, the Daily Mail reports. The 22-year-old is believed to be on the radar of several clubs in Spain amid struggles to earn a place in Unai Emery's side, with 32 minutes of action in the Premier League spread across three substitute appearances. He is on loan from Chelsea, but any potential permanent move at Villa Park would require conditions to be met, which would see a £43 million proposed deal become official.

articles.headline: Sources: Mavs' Dereck Lively II (foot) not cleared for camp
articles.description: Dereck Lively II's status for the start of the season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources said.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN on Wednesday.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the past 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress.

Dallas begins training camp Saturday.

Lively has played a total of only 43 games in the past two seasons. He underwent his second surgery in December, ending his 2025-26 season after appearing in only seven games.

Lively, 22, the No. 12 pick in the 2023 draft, is entering the final season of his rookie contract.

If healthy, the 7-foot-1, 230-pound Lively could be a significant part of Dallas' long-term core as the Mavericks attempt to build a contender around reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

Lively, an athletic big man who is an excellent finisher and versatile defender, has career averages of 8.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 22.9 minutes.

articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Sept. 23

Sources: Status of Mavs big man Lively up in air

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

Extension unlikely as Knicks, Towns talks stall

Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Vincent Goodwill on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

Sept. 22

Charania: Hield, Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith

The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
